names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 4 mai, «Sfânta Muceniță Pelaghia».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 4 Μαΐου, «Αγία Πελαγία», with the rank word left off.

The bare name out of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 2643 and the heading of both of its lives for her, «Мученица Пелагия Тарсийская», with the rank word and the epithet left off. The longer life gives «Пелагея» in the same breath as «Пелагия» and is not followed.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 4. мај ст. ст., „Света мученица Пелагија Тарсанка.“ Света is no rank and мученица is the `martyr` this folder already carries in `types` and `honorific.js` composes back, so both are stripped; **Тарсанка is kept** — the woman of Tarsus, an ethnic by-name and not a rank the composer adds back, as Острошки, Боровски and Кијево-Печерски were kept on earlier days of this wave. Keeping it is what holds this folder **out** of the bare «Пелагија» that `pelagia-of-caesarea-in-palestine` holds, which was measured and not assumed.

feast.note: Her two life pages both head «Дни памяти: 4 мая , 7 октября», and the Russian calendar keeps her on both; 4 May is the day the Greek and the Romanian keep her on as well. One row per church is the schema, so the May day is recorded here and she does not render on it. The 7 October page also points at a service «4 мая: Преподобномученицы Пелагии», which is the May day's.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, 7 октября ст. ст. — «Мц. Пелагии Тарсийской (290).»
source.note: No rank is recorded. Her line stands in the day's second paragraph, which carries no icon; the day's one icon, «Совершается служба на шесть», stands before the martyrs Sergius and Bacchus in the first.

attestations.note: The two lives the site reaches for her disagree on the year — 287 on the shorter, 290 on the longer and on the day line — and they also tell the story differently: the shorter has her mother hand her to the rejected bridegroom and the emperor want her married to his heir, the longer has bishop Clinon, the baptism at the spring and the four lions. The folder's `dates` carry both years and neither is preferred.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 4 mai — «Sfânta Muceniță Pelaghia»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 4ης Μαΐου — «Αγία Πελαγία»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 4 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps her, and it is plainly the same virgin martyr: of Tarsus, under Diocletian, burnt inside a heated brazen ox. **The Greek adds the whole story the folder did not have** — the vision of the bishop of Rome who told her to be baptised, the pretext of visiting her nurse, the fine clothes handed to the bishop to be sold for the poor, the nurse and then the mother driving her out, the suicide of Diocletian's son to whom she was betrothed, and the emperor's order for the brazen ox — and **the relics**: «Αποτμήματα του Ιερού Λειψάνου της Αγίας φυλάσσονται στις Μονές Μεγ. Λαύρας Αγίου Όρους, Προυσού Ευρυτανίας και Νταού Πεντέλης και στό Ναό του Αγίου Γεωργίου των Ελλήνων Βενετίας.» **It prints no year**, so `dates` stays absent. **Its geography is its own slip and is left alone**: «γεννήθηκε στην πόλη Ταρσό της Κιλκισίας», Tarsus of Kilkisia, where Κιλικίας, Cilicia, is meant — Kilkis is a town in Macedonia — and it then says she lived at Rome, which the Romanian account does not. Both are printed here without being corrected. **The apolytikion in Ἦχος γ’ is proper and names her** and is stored; the folder's Romanian troparion is a different text. The bishop of Rome the page names is unnamed, so there is no `related` row.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 17.05.2026 (4. мај ст. ст.) — „Света мученица Пелагија Тарсанка.“

attestations.note: **The day is Julian 4 May, with the Romanian and the Greek; the Russian keeps her on 7 октября, and that row was not moved.** **No date was changed, and the reason is that the interval already holds this book's year.** Her `death` is 287–290, „287 or 290“, because the Sretensky site's two lives disagree with each other; „Пострада чесно 287. године“ is the earlier of those two readings, so the Prologue is now **a second source for 287 against 290** and **the interval was deliberately not narrowed to it** — narrowing a sourced interval is not a reader's act, and the disagreement the Russian reader recorded is still a disagreement. New besides, and this is the fullest account of her read for this folder: that her parents were pagan but **notable and rich**; that **Diocletian himself halted at Tarsus** and that it was during that stay that his son fell mortally in love with her; that she answered the prince **through her own wicked mother**, that she was already promised to her heavenly Bridegroom; that fleeing both of them she sought out and found **the bishop Clinon**, a man notable for his holiness, who taught her the faith and baptised her; that she then gave away her sumptuous clothes and much wealth, went home and confessed the baptism to her mother; that **the emperor's son ran himself through with a sword** when he lost all hope of her; that **her own mother laid the accusation** before the emperor and handed her over to judgement; that the emperor, forgetting his son, burned with an unclean passion for her himself and, when she would not be moved, condemned her to be burnt **in a metal ox heated by fire**; that when the torturers stripped her she crossed herself and **walked into the glowing ox of her own accord**, with a prayer of thanksgiving on her lips, and in the twinkling of an eye melted away in it like wax; that **the bishop Clinon obtained what was left of her bones and buried them on a hill under a stone**; and that in the time of „цара Константина Копронима (741-775)“ a beautiful church was built on that spot in her honour. The bishop Clinon has **no folder in this corpus** — checked by listing every folder whose name reads like it — so he is named in the life with no `related` row, and the emperor Constantine Copronymus is a persecuting reign and no saint. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mieluşeaua Ta, Iisuse, Pelaghia, strigă cu glas mare: pe Tine, Mirele meu, te iubesc și pe Tine căutându-Te mă chinuiesc și împreună mă răstignesc, și împreună mă îngrop cu Botezul Tău; și pătimesc pentru Tine, ca să împărățesc întru Tine; și mor pentru tine, ca să viez pentru Tine; ci, ca o jertfă fără de prihană, primește/mă pe mine ceea ce cu dragoste mă jertfesc Ție. Pentru rugăciunile ei, ca un milostiv, mântuiește sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfintei Mucenițe Pelaghia din Tars», Glasul 4; the reading «primește/mă» is the page's own

english.text: Thy ewe-lamb, O Jesus, Pelagia, cries out with a great voice: Thee, my Bridegroom, I love, and seeking Thee I am in torment; I am crucified with Thee and buried with Thee in Thy baptism; I suffer for Thee that I may reign in Thee, and I die for Thee that I may live for Thee. Receive me as a sacrifice without spot, who offer myself to Thee in love. At her prayers, in Thy mercy, save our souls.

hymns.text: Θείας πίστεως, τὴ ἐπιγνώσει, ζόφον ἔλιπες, τῆς ἀγνωσίας, Πελαγία Χριστοῦ, καλλιπάρθενε. Οὐ τὴν ἀείζωον δρόσον πλουτήσασα, διὰ πυρὸς τὸν ἀγῶνα ἐτέλεσας. Μάρτυς ἔνδοξε, Χριστὸν τὸν Θεὸν ἱκέτευε, δωρήσασθαι ἠμὶν τὸ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος γ’, Θείας πίστεως, on the page of «Αγία Πελαγία»

english.text: By the knowledge of the divine faith thou didst leave the gloom of ignorance, O Pelagia, fair virgin of Christ. Made rich with the ever-living dew, thou didst finish thy contest through fire. O glorious martyr, entreat Christ our God to grant us great mercy.

death.note: The site's two lives for her disagree and neither is preferred. The shorter says «предала Богу душу в 287 году»; the longer says «Мучения и смерть святой Пелагии произошли в 290 году», which is also the year the calendar's day line prints.
